title: Low-leakage reference: a low-capacity victim with real members shows little measured leakage

invariants.description: Unlike the placebo, half of the candidates are ACTUAL training members of this victim (250/500), under the membership contract.

Measured threshold-attack AUC against real members must stay ≤ 0.6 (observed 0.511; 20-seed range 0.464–0.555 over both label settings). An empirical result for this model and data, not a privacy guarantee.
Measured shadow-attack AUC must stay ≤ 0.6 (observed 0.468; 20-seed range 0.438–0.557).
Threshold advantage TPR − FPR must stay ≤ 0.15 (observed 0.024; 20-seed range −0.044 to +0.060).
Shadow advantage must stay ≤ 0.15 (observed 0.012; 20-seed range −0.060 to +0.100).
The low-capacity model barely overfits (observed gap −0.013; 20-seed range −0.063 to +0.062).

rationale: The genuine negative-direction reference: the same attacker knowledge, candidates and outputs as MLB-REG-019, but a victim whose small generalisation gap leaves little membership signal. Its absence of leakage is NOT assumed: leakage is tested on real members and non-members each run, and was claimed on 2 of 20 seeds in each 20-seed study (no claim at seed 7), so no invariant asserts 'no leakage'.
